headline: Nigeria Powers 50,000 People With 23 New Solar Mini-Grids
meta_description: Nigeria has completed 23 solar mini-grids with UN support, bringing electricity to 50,000 people across more than 20,000 households in rural areas.
summary_short: With UN development backing, Nigeria has finished building 23 solar mini-grids now fully operational, electrifying rural communities and 50,000 residents.
body:
Nigeria has completed 23 solar mini-grids with UN development support, and all are now 100% operational. The achievement brings electricity to 50,000 people across more than 20,000 households in rural areas, marking a significant step toward energy access across the country.

The project demonstrates how targeted renewable infrastructure, paired with international development assistance, can reach underserved communities. By deploying solar mini-grids rather than relying on centralized power systems, Nigeria is expanding electricity access to remote regions where traditional grid extension would be prohibitively expensive.

These operational mini-grids now power rural businesses and households, enabling economic activity and improving living standards in communities that previously lacked reliable electricity.
